name: patch_aob
description: Cheat-Engine-style Array-of-Bytes (AOB) scan followed by a one-shot memory patch. Attacker enumerates the target's committed memory regions, ReadProcessMemory each one, searches for a byte pattern locally, and only writes to the first match. Distinctive fingerprint vs. patch_direct: the scan produces many cross-process READVM_REMOTE events (one per region touched — typically dozens for a game process) before a single WRITEVM_REMOTE. This is the canonical Cheat-Engine workflow: 'Scan for value → filter → add to address list → edit'. No allocation, no protection change, no thread manipulation — just read-heavy reconnaissance followed by one direct write.

extra.expected_fingerprint: MANY cross-process READVM_REMOTE events (one per committed memory region scanned in the target — count depends on target's VAD layout, typically 30-100+ for a real game), 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (the actual patch after the pattern is located), 1x READVM_REMOTE (the --verify read-back). Notably absent: 0x ALLOCVM_REMOTE, 0x PROTECTVM_REMOTE, 0x THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE, 0x SETTHREADCONTEXT. The read/write ratio is the discriminator vs. all other techniques in the corpus.
